Choose a subclass:

All Chieftain's Presence Commander's Presence Dancer's Presence Dreadlord's Presence Noble's Presence Packleader's Presence Paragon's Presence Tactician's Presence

Chieftain's Presence

A chieftain is a Warlord who rules by the sheer force of their personality. Marked by their booming voice and fearless attitude, it is easy for their band to believe they are infallible while their chieftain stands.

They may be lawful or chaotic, good or evil, depending on how they came to power. An orc who carved their way to the top may be chaotic, believing that strength should rise unfettered by rules, while someone who inherited authority may lean toward a more lawful outlook.

A Warlord with the Presence of a Chieftain need not literally rule anything, but embodies someone who has — or could — walk that path through overwhelming charisma and the boisterous inspiration they lend to those around them.

docs.title: Hit Points
docs.text: Hit Dice: 1d8 per Warlord level Hit Points at 1st Level: 8 + your Constitution modifier Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d8 (5) + your Constitution modifier per Warlord level after 1st

docs.title: Proficiencies
docs.text:
Armor: Light armor, medium armor Weapons: Simple weapons Tools: None

Saving Throws: Wisdom, Charisma Skills: Choose three from Athletics, Deception, History, Insight, Intimidation, Investigation, Medicine, Performance, and Persuasion

docs.title: Equipment
docs.text:
You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

  • (a) a simple melee weapon, or (b) a martial weapon (if proficient)
  • (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts, or (b) a shield (if proficient)
  • (a) leather armor, or (b) scale mail, or (c) chain mail (if proficient)
  • (a) a scholar's pack or (b) an explorer's pack

docs.title: Level 1 – Warlord Presences
docs.text: At 1st level, you pick the archetype of Warlord you embody, called a Presence, choosing from Commander, Chieftain, Noble, Packleader, Paragon, or Tactician, each of which is detailed at the end of the class description. Your Presence grants you features at 1st level, and again at 3rd, 7th, 11th, 15th, and 18th level.

docs.title: Level 1 – Battlefield Presence
docs.text:
Starting at 1st level, when you take the Attack action, in place of making an attack, you can use your Battlefield Presence to grant a friendly creature that can see or hear you an additional attack the next time they take the Attack action during their turn.

Any additional attacks granted that are unused at the start of your next turn are lost. A friendly creature can only gain one additional attack per round from this feature.

docs.title: Level 2 – Leadership Dice
docs.text:
Starting at 2nd level, you have access to Leadership Dice. These represent your ability to focus your battlefield presence for powerful results. Your Warlord level determines the number and size of the dice, as shown on the Leadership Dice column of the Warlord table. You can spend these to fuel various features.

You know three such features: Rallying Mark, Urgent Orders, and Helpful Word. When you gain this feature, you can spend one Leadership Die per turn. Starting at 6th level, you can spend two Leadership Dice per turn. The number you can expend increases to three at 11th level, and to four at 17th level.

A Leadership Die is expended when you use it. You regain all expended Leadership Dice when you finish a short or long rest.

Rallying Mark. As a bonus action, you can expend a number of Leadership Dice (up to your per turn limit) to rally your allies to attack a hostile creature within 60 feet of you.

The next time damage is rolled against that target by an allied creature before the start of your next turn, they can add the Leadership Dice to the damage roll, and the attacking creature regains hit points equal to the amount rolled.

Urgent Orders. As a bonus action, you can expend a number of Leadership Dice (up to your per turn limit) to guide your allies in expeditious action.

Target an allied creature within 60 feet of you that can see or hear you. That creature can immediately use its reaction to move up to its movement speed (up to 30 feet) without provoking opportunity attacks. Roll the Leadership Dice expended; the target gains temporary hit points equal to the value rolled.

Helpful Word. As a bonus action, you can expend a Leadership Die to take the Help action. When you use the Help action to aid an ally in attacking a creature, the target of that attack can be within 30 feet of you—rather than within 5 feet—if your ally can see or hear you.

docs.title: Level 3 – Warlord’s Expertise
docs.text: Starting at 3rd level, choose one of the following skills: Investigation, Insight, Intimidation, or Persuasion. If you are not proficient in the chosen skill, you become proficient. If you are already proficient in the chosen skill, your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with that skill.

docs.title: Level 4 – Ability Score Improvement
docs.text: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

docs.title: Level 5 – Extra Attack
docs.text: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. You can use Battlefield Presence in place of either or both attacks.

docs.title: Level 6 – Prepare for Battle
docs.text:
Starting at 6th level, you can spend a minute preparing creatures for combat. You can expend a number of Leadership Dice up to your per-turn limit, rolling them and causing up to five creatures of your choice (including yourself, if you choose) to gain temporary hit points equal to the number rolled.

Allies that benefit from this ability can expend a number of Hit Dice equal to the number of Leadership Dice you expended, using them as they would during a short rest. Any temporary hit points gained this way last until you complete a short or long rest.

docs.title: Level 9 – Press the Attack
docs.text:
Starting at 9th level, your abilities are further empowered.

Rallying Mark: Boost Morale. When a creature gains hit points from Rallying Mark, you can use your reaction to expend one Leadership Die to cause another creature within 60 feet of the attacker to regain the same number of hit points.

Urgent Orders: Coordinated Movements. When you use Urgent Orders, you can expend additional Leadership Dice to target additional creatures (one additional creature per extra die spent).

Helpful Word: Expert Instructions. When a creature benefits from your Help action, you can use your reaction to expend a Leadership Die and add it to their roll. You can use this ability after the roll is made, but before the outcome is known.

docs.title: Level 13 – Warlord’s Intuition
docs.text: Starting at 13th level, before rolling an ability check you are proficient in, you can choose for the d20 roll to equal your Warlord level instead of rolling. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

docs.title: Level 14 – Shift the Field
docs.text: Starting at 14th level, you gain the ability to relocate friendly creatures. As an action, you can expend one Leadership Die to move up to five friendly creatures that can see or hear you up to half their movement speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

docs.title: Level 17 – Unbreakable Will
docs.text:
Starting at 17th level, you are immune to the frightened and charmed conditions.

Commander's Presence

A Commander on the field can be many things — a trusted sergeant, a weary veteran, or merely a person with an uncommon degree of common sense and a particularly keen eye for how to win a fight.

While not as flashy as some of the other Presences on the battlefield, that just means they are less likely to get themselves skewered. A keen word there and a helping hand here, their influence is subtle but effective, inexorably shifting the tides of battle in their favor.

A Commander can come from any background, but is usually someone that has acquired their Wisdom the hard way, having seen a bit of what life and battlefields have to offer.

Dancer's Presence

A unique presence on the battlefield, these graceful agents wind their way through death and destruction with a curious elegance, uplifting their allies and distracting their enemies. A dancer comes in many forms, be they prancing jesters or graceful enchanters, their presence seems supernaturally captivating to all who encounter them, for good or ill. Though they seem out of place in danger, confused onlookers will often find them as the last ones standing in the most dangerous of situations, always one step out of out the greatest danger.

Dreadlord's Presence

A warlord that follows this path specializes in terror and fear, usually localized to their enemies. While other warlords look to boost and inspire their allies, a Dreadlord works to undermine and terrify their enemies, crushing their will to fight and leaving them as prey easily slaughtered.

A Dreadlord is not always evil, though they most often appear in the ranks of evil, but by their very nature they are someone who can instill dread and terror. The source of this dread can be a cursed visage, supernatural gift, or simply a tyrannical force of will.

Noble's Presence

A Warlord with a Noble Presence is not inherently one born to nobility, though many are. A Noble Presence Warlord is one who drives their retainers and companions to greater heights through sheer charisma, standing beside them as a shining beacon of what they fight for.

From time immemorial, soldiers have fought twice as hard when their leader joins them on the battlefield, pushing themselves to impossible limits to protect their liege. An adventurer of this path may or may not be such a liege, but their charisma inspires the same fervor in their companions.

A Noble Presence Warlord is not always of noble birth, though many are. A noble raised on the laws of the land is usually lawful, though extraordinary circumstances may foster rebellion against unfit rulers — or rulers who are merely inconvenient.

Packleader's Presence

While Warlords may specialize in controlling battles, a Packleader aims to win the fight before it becomes one. Through scouting, preparation, and stacking the odds, they do not fight fair — they fight to win, and seek to fight only when the battle is already theirs.

Their influence extends beyond allies on the field, shaping the battlefield itself to hinder foes and conceal companions. Though good or evil rarely guides a Packleader’s philosophy, they tend to be Chaotic, viewing “rules of engagement” and civilized conventions as weaknesses to exploit rather than norms to follow.

Paragon's Presence

Legends tell of warriors that fight at the front of a legion, of the valor they display and the inspiration it gives their comrades. A Paragon before their army is a dauntless foe, and an army behind their Paragon is an unstoppable legion.

A Paragon is not inherently good or evil. An evil legion can be led by a bold and charismatic Warlord just as effectively as the forces of good. As they tend to be those that inspire an organized force, more often than not they will be lawful, but what that personal code of laws entails can vary quite widely.

Tactician's Presence

A Tactician may very well tell you they would just as soon not be close enough to the battle to be considered a combatant, preferring to win their fights before they even reach that stage, but one would be a fool to underestimate how dangerous they are once on the battlefield.

While they might have laid their plans in advance, their sharp minds can quickly pick apart how their foes try to fight against them and effortlessly pierce the crude tactics that would be used against them and their allies. What tends to mark a Tactician is a keen mind and a willingness to plan ahead... in great detail. Adventurers with a tactician among them are near impossible to pin down, as they will always find a way to turn the tables.

docs.title: Level 20 – Tireless Leader
docs.text: Starting at 20th level, you can roll d4s and use them instead of expending Leadership Dice for Rallying Mark, Urgent Orders, Helpful Word, or Prepare for Battle.

docs.title: Level 1 – Chieftain's Proficiency
docs.text: Starting at 1st level when you take this Presence, you gain proficiency in shields, martial weapons, and the Intimidation skill. If you are already proficient in Intimidation, you instead gain proficiency in another skill of your choice.

docs.title: Level 1 – Wolfpack Movement
docs.text: Starting at 1st level, the first time an allied creature moves, it can bring a number of willing creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) within 20 feet of you, moving them the same distance and direction. These creatures cannot move more than half their movement speed and cannot move more than 20 feet from you. Each creature may stop its movement at any point along the path.

docs.title: Level 3 – Warcry
docs.text:
Starting at 3rd level, as an action or in place of one attack when you take the Attack action, you can expend a number of Leadership Dice (up to your per-turn limit) to unleash a mighty Warcry. You and friendly creatures within 20 feet of you gain temporary hit points equal to the Leadership Dice roll + your Charisma modifier (minimum 1). This can affect a number of creatures up to 1 + your Charisma modifier (minimum 1).

After using Warcry, you may make a single weapon attack as a bonus action. This attack has disadvantage unless made with a weapon that has the light property.

docs.title: Level 3 – Savage Momentum
docs.text: Additionally at 3rd level, whenever you spend a Leadership Die, you gain advantage on the next attack roll you make before the end of your turn.

docs.title: Level 7 – Reckless Assault
docs.text: Starting at 7th level, when a creature with temporary hit points granted by one of your abilities deals damage, it may expend any amount of those temporary hit points to add extra damage equal to half the temporary hit points spent (rounded down).

docs.title: Level 11 – Wolfpack Tactics
docs.text:
Starting at 11th level, you excel at coordinated takedowns. The first creature you hit that has taken damage from one of your allies since the end of your last turn takes an additional 1d12 damage.

Additionally, the first time a creature you grant an attack through Battlefield Presence deals damage to a creature you damaged on your turn, that attack deals an additional 1d4 damage.

docs.title: Level 15 – Booming Shout
docs.text:
Starting at 15th level, when you unleash your Warcry you may attempt to frighten enemies. Any number of creatures of your choice within the Warcry’s range must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus) or become frightened of you until the end of their next turn. Once you use Booming Shout, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

Additionally, the range of your Rallying Mark, Urgent Orders, Helpful Word, and Warcry is doubled.

docs.title: Level 18 – Bloody Victory
docs.text:
Starting at 18th level, when you or an ally reduces a creature that has dealt damage to you to 0 hit points, you can unleash a Warcry as a reaction. When you unleash your Warcry in this way, you do not expend any Leadership Dice, and you use a d12 instead of your normal Leadership Die.

You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, regaining all uses when you finish a long rest.

docs.title: Level 1 – Martial Proficiency
docs.text: Starting at 1st level when you take this Presence, you gain proficiency in heavy armor, shields, and martial weapons.

docs.title: Level 1 – Form Up!
docs.text: Starting at 1st level, when you roll initiative and are not surprised, any number of friendly creatures within 30 feet of you can move up to their speed a number of feet equal to five times your Wisdom modifier (minimum 5 feet).

docs.title: Level 3 – Keen Pointer
docs.text:
Starting at 3rd level, you can take the Helpful Word bonus action without expending a Leadership Die if you are within 5 feet of the creature you are taking the Help action against.

When you do so, you can expend Leadership Dice to apply Rallying Mark to the creature you are targeting with this Help action.

docs.title: Level 7 – On Your Feet!
docs.text:
Starting at 7th level, you can use a bonus action and expend one Leadership Die to restore the will to fight in an allied creature. Choose a friendly creature within 5 feet of you. That creature regains hit points equal to your Leadership Die.

When you use this feature to restore hit points to a creature at 0 hit points, you can add your Wisdom modifier to the amount of hit points restored. If the creature is prone, it can choose to stand immediately.

docs.title: Level 11 – Martial Advantage
docs.text: Starting at 11th level, you've learned to leverage fighting alongside an ally. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 2d6 damage to a creature you hit with a weapon attack if that creature is within 5 feet of an ally that isn't incapacitated.

docs.title: Level 15 – Bulwark
docs.text: Starting at 15th level, when you and any number of friendly creatures within 30 feet of you make a saving throw against the same effect, your allies gain advantage on their saving throw if you succeed on the saving throw.

docs.title: Level 18 – No One Left Behind!
docs.text: Starting at 18th level, you can move up to your speed to get within 5 feet of a creature while using your On Your Feet! feature. During this movement, you gain resistance to all damage, and the target regains an additional 1d8 hit points for each attack of opportunity made against you during this movement.

docs.title: Level 1 – Dancer's Grace
docs.text:
Starting at 1st level when you take this Presence, you gain proficiency with Performance. If you already have proficiency with performance, you gain expertise with it, meaning you can add twice your proficiency modifier to checks made with it.

Additionally, while you are not wearing armor or carrying a shield, you gain an unarmored defense that is 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Charisma modifier.

docs.title: Level 1 – Graceful Entrance
docs.text: Starting at 1st level, you can give yourself a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to your Charisma modifier. Additionally when you roll initiative and are not surprised, you can move up to your half movement speed, and you and any creature you end this movement within 5 feet of gains temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier.

docs.title: Level 3 – Bewildering Steps
docs.text: At 3rd level, you gain an additional use for leadership dice.

docs.title: Level 3 – Distract
docs.text: As a bonus action, you attempt to distract a creature within 30 feet. Until the start of its next turn, if that creature attacks a creature other than you while you are within range of its attack, you can roll your leadership die and subtract it from their attack.

docs.title: Level 3 – Dancer's Dodge
docs.text:
Starting at 3rd level, when you take the Dodge action while you are not wearing armor or carrying a shield, you can use Distract, Helpful Word, Urgent Orders, or Rallying Mark without expending a leadership die. When you do so, it applies as if you had spent 1 leadership die on it for its effect.

Additionally, when you take the Dodge action, you can expend leadership dice to grant attacks through Battlefield Presence. You can grant a number of attacks equal to the leadership dice spent, up to your per turn limit.

docs.title: Level 7 – Battlefield Grace
docs.text: Starting at 7th level, whenever a creature misses you with an attack, you regain 1 spent leadership die and can move 5 feet. You cannot regain a leadership die this way again until the start of your next turn.

docs.title: Level 7 – Whirling Thorns
docs.text: Additionally at 7th level, if you are carrying a melee weapon with the light property, you can make a single attack with it as a bonus action. You can expend leadership dice to make additional attacks as part of the same action, but each attack must be against a different target within range.

docs.title: Level 11 – Furious Tempo
docs.text: Starting at 11th level, you can add your Charisma modifier to the damage of attacks you make or grant through Battlefield Presence.

docs.title: Level 15 – Evasion
docs.text: Starting at 15th level, you can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain area effects. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

docs.title: Level 18 – Elegant Exchange
docs.text: Starting at 18th level, when a willing creature within 15 feet of you is the target of a spell, attack, or targeted effect that would cause them to take damage, you can move their position as a reaction, moving them 5 feet in any direction and becoming the target of the attack.

docs.title: Level 1 – Dreadlord Proficiency
docs.text: Starting at 1st level when you select this Presence, you gain proficiency in heavy armor and the Intimidation skill.

docs.title: Level 1 – Unapproachable
docs.text: Additionally at 1st level, your intimidating presence causes your foes to falter at the start of combat. After rolling initiative, the first attack by the first hostile creature to attack an allied creature within 30 feet of you has disadvantage.

docs.title: Level 3 – Demoralization Dice
docs.text:
Starting at 3rd level, whenever you spend a Leadership Die, you gain a Demoralization Die of equal size. Demoralization Dice last until you have gone 1 minute without earning or spending one. You can spend Demoralization Dice as a reaction for one of the following effects:

Make it Excruciating. When a creature within 30 feet of you takes damage from a weapon attack made by an ally, you can expend Demoralization Dice (up to your Leadership Die limit), rolling them and causing the target to take additional damage equal to the value rolled.

Don't Touch That. When a creature attacks an allied creature within 30 feet of you, you can expend one Demoralization Die, rolling it and reducing the attacker's attack roll.

Are You Sure? When a creature ends its turn within 5 feet of you, you can expend Demoralization Dice (up to your Leadership Die limit) and force the creature to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus). On failure, the creature uses its reaction to move a number of feet away from you equal to 10 × the Demoralization Dice spent. The target automatically succeeds if immune to the frightened condition.

docs.title: Level 7 – Supernatural Dread
docs.text:
Starting at 7th level, you can use Leadership Dice (up to your per-turn limit) to cast frighten without a spell slot. The level of the spell equals the number of Leadership Dice spent.

Alternatively, you can spend 3 Leadership Dice (even if it exceeds your per-turn limit) to cast fear without expending a spell slot or material component once per long rest.

Charisma is your spellcasting modifier for these spells.

docs.title: Level 7 – Iron Mask
docs.text:
Additionally at 7th level, you are exceptionally good at masking your emotions. Creatures have disadvantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks against you.

You can also suppress the frightened condition on yourself, requiring concentration as if concentrating on a spell. You cannot maintain this effect while concentrating on another spell.

docs.title: Level 11 – Punish the Weak
docs.text:
Starting at 11th level, when you target a creature within 60 feet with any ability, feature, or attack, you can mark them for punishment (no action required). The mark lasts until the creature ends its turn more than 60 feet from you, dies, or you mark another creature.

Once per turn, when the marked creature takes damage, it takes an additional 1d8 damage. This increases to 1d12 if the target is frightened of you.

docs.title: Level 15 – Instinctive Flinch
docs.text: Starting at 15th level, when a creature passes a Wisdom saving throw against one of your features that would cause them to become frightened or flee, they still have disadvantage on their next attack roll made before the start of your next turn. This has no effect if the target is immune to the frightened condition.

docs.title: Level 15 – Expanded Dominion
docs.text: Additionally at 15th level, the range of your Demoralization Dice effects is doubled (making them 60 feet, 60 feet, and 10 feet, respectively).

docs.title: Level 18 – Dreadful Terror
docs.text:
Starting at 18th level, when a target becomes frightened of you, you can expend Demoralization Dice to enhance the effect (no action required):

Panicked Terror. The target immediately spends its reaction to move up to half its movement speed away from you.

Blind Terror. You can expend 2 Demoralization Dice to cause the target to become blinded until the start of your next turn.

Paralyzing Terror. You can expend 3 Demoralization Dice to cause the target to become paralyzed until the start of your next turn.

docs.title: Level 1 – Destined Leader
docs.text:
Starting at 1st level when you take this Presence, you gain proficiency with rapiers, longswords, and the Persuasion skill. If you are already proficient in Persuasion, you instead gain proficiency in another skill of your choice.

Additionally, you gain an additional Leadership Die at 3rd level, 9th level, and 15th level.

docs.title: Level 1 – Call to Arms
docs.text: Starting at 1st level, when you roll initiative you may call out to friendly creatures within 60 feet of you, granting them a surge of inspiration. Creatures of your choice equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) gain advantage on their first attack roll in the combat.

docs.title: Level 1 – Inspiring Leader
docs.text: Additionally at 1st level, an allied creature with a CR less than half your Warlord level (or with fewer class levels than your Warlord level, if it has no CR) may choose to use your proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier as the attack roll modifier on the first attack they make in a turn granted by your Battlefield Presence.

docs.title: Level 3 – Divine Right
docs.text:
Starting at 3rd level, you may expend Leadership Dice (up to your per-turn limit) to cast command. The spell’s level equals the number of Leadership Dice spent.

The spell save DC for these spells is 8 + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus.

You may also add your Charisma modifier (maximum +2) to your AC while you are not wearing heavy armor or using a shield.

docs.title: Level 3 – Charismatic Leadership
docs.text:
Additionally at 3rd level, you may add your Charisma modifier to:

  • The damage bonus of Rallying Mark,
  • The temporary hit points granted by Urgent Orders, and
  • The attack roll of a creature that gains advantage from Helpful Word.

docs.title: Level 7 – Words of Conviction
docs.text: Starting at 7th level, you may expend Leadership Dice (up to your per-turn limit) to cast bless or heroism without material components. The spell’s level equals the number of Leadership Dice spent.

docs.title: Level 7 – Imperative Order
docs.text:
Starting at 7th level, when you spend 2 or more Leadership Dice on a target with Urgent Orders, the creature may make a single weapon attack with its reaction instead of moving.

If you spend 3 or more Leadership Dice, the creature may both move and make a single weapon attack with its reaction.

docs.title: Level 11 – Inspired Zeal
docs.text: Starting at 11th level, all creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you deal an extra 1d4 radiant damage when they hit with a weapon attack.

docs.title: Level 15 – Untouchable Presence
docs.text:
Starting at 15th level, you are under the effect of the sanctuary spell. This effect ends normally if you take an action that would break it, but it returns at the start of your next turn.

The spell save DC is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier.

docs.title: Level 18 – Grand Decree
docs.text:
Starting at 18th level, you can cast command without expending a spell slot or Leadership Dice. When you do, the spell affects all creatures of your choice within range who are valid targets.

Once you cast command using this ability, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

docs.title: Level 1 – Tools of the Wild
docs.text:
Starting at 1st level when you take this Presence, you gain proficiency in martial weapons and in the Survival skill. If you are already proficient in Survival, you instead gain proficiency in another skill of your choice.

Additionally, you gain proficiency with your choice of the Herbalism Kit or the Poisoner’s Kit.

docs.title: Level 1 – Concealed Approach
docs.text:
Starting at 1st level, if you have at least 1 minute to prepare, you may add your Wisdom modifier to a Dexterity (Stealth) check made by you and up to five friendly creatures.

You and friendly creatures within 30 feet of you who roll initiative while hidden may also add your Wisdom modifier to the initiative roll.

docs.title: Level 3 – Nature’s Gift
docs.text:
Starting at 3rd level, you learn the mold earth cantrip and one additional Druid cantrip of your choice.

Additionally, you may expend one Leadership Die to cast fog cloud or snare as a 1st-level spell. When casting snare in this way, its casting time is 1 action.

You also choose one additional 1st-level Druid spell with a casting time of 1 action; you may cast this spell by expending one Leadership Die.

Your spellcasting modifier for these spells is Wisdom, and the spell save DC is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier.

docs.title: Level 7 – Shroud of Nature
docs.text: Starting at 7th level, whenever you cast a spell that causes you or a friendly creature to become obscured (such as being within fog cloud or behind terrain altered by mold earth), the obscured creature may use its reaction to take the Hide action.

docs.title: Level 7 – Trackless Trails
docs.text: Additionally at 7th level, you may expend 2 Leadership Dice to cast pass without trace without requiring material components.

docs.title: Level 11 – Fleeting Strikers
docs.text:
Starting at 11th level, if you are not in the same space you occupied at the end of your last turn, or you are obscured from your target, the first attack you make on your turn deals an additional 1d10 damage.

Additionally, a creature you grant an attack through Battlefield Presence may choose to take the Dash action instead of making the attack you granted.

docs.title: Level 15 – Ghosts of the Wild
docs.text:
Starting at 15th level, while under the effect of pass without trace, you may expend one Leadership Die to take the Hide action at the end of your turn without using an action.

If you use Battlefield Presence to grant a creature an attack, you may expend one Leadership Die to shroud them in shadows or natural phenomena, granting advantage on the first attack they make before the start of your next turn.

If the target is under pass without trace, you may do this without expending a Leadership Die.

docs.title: Level 18 – Warlord of the Wilds
docs.text:
Starting at 18th level, you may choose five additional spells from the Druid spell list of 4th level or lower. You may cast these spells by expending Leadership Dice equal to the spell’s level.

You may change your selected spells when you complete a long rest.

The spell save DC for these spells is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier.

Whenever you expend Leadership Dice to cast a spell, you may take the Attack action as a bonus action (one weapon attack only).

docs.title: Level 1 – Martial Proficiency
docs.text: Starting at 1st level when you take this Presence, you gain proficiency in heavy armor, shields, and martial weapons.

docs.title: Level 1 – Lead the Charge
docs.text: Starting at 1st level, you can give yourself a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to your Charisma modifier. Additionally, when you roll initiative you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus.

docs.title: Level 3 – Fighting Style
docs.text:
Starting at 3rd level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can’t take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

Defense. While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

Dueling. When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

Great Weapon Fighting. When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.

Two-Weapon Fighting. When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

docs.title: Level 3 – Heroic Strike
docs.text:
Additionally at 3rd level, when you take the Attack action, once per turn you can expend Leadership Dice (up to your per turn limit) to apply Rallying Mark as part of a melee weapon attack.

Whenever you expend Leadership Dice as part of making an attack, you can add the expended Leadership Dice to the damage roll of the attack.

docs.title: Level 7 – Stand Defiant
docs.text: Starting at 7th level, when you are reduced to zero hit points, you instantly regain a number of hit points equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1). Additionally, you can expend a number of Leadership Dice equal to the number of friendly creatures within 60 feet of you, regaining additional hit points equal to the value rolled this way. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

docs.title: Level 11 – Inspired Warrior
docs.text:
Starting at 11th level, once per turn, when one of your allies within 30 feet takes or deals damage, you gain d4 dice, adding it to a pool of dice. You can have a maximum number of d4 dice in this pool equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1).

Until the end of your next turn, when you deal damage you can expend any number of dice from this pool, rolling them and dealing additional damage equal to the value rolled.

docs.title: Level 15 – Dauntless Resolve
docs.text: Starting at 15th level, when you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. Once you do this, you cannot do this again until you complete a long rest.

docs.title: Level 18 – Invincible Legion
docs.text:
Starting at 18th level, your allies will never fall so long as their symbol of hope remains. When a friendly creature within 60 feet of you is reduced to 0 hit points, but not killed outright, they can drop to 1 hit point instead so long as they can see or hear you.

Once a creature benefits from this effect, they cannot benefit from it again until they complete a long rest.

docs.title: Level 1 – Tactician's Cunning
docs.text: When you take this Presence at 1st level, you gain proficiency in the History and Investigation skills, or other skills of your choice if you are already proficient. Additionally, if you can take a minute or more making a skill check, you can treat a d20 roll of 4 or lower as a 5.

docs.title: Level 1 – Battle Plans
docs.text: Starting at 1st level, you can give yourself a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to your Intelligence modifier. Additionally, you can exchange your initiative roll with a willing friendly creature within 60 feet.

docs.title: Level 3 – Tactical Insight
docs.text:
Starting at 3rd level, you can tactically assess a creature's options. As a bonus action, make an Intelligence (Investigation) check contested by a Charisma (Deception) check against any creature you can see within 60 feet.

On a success, you can see through their tactics, granting one of the following effects:

Determine Attack. You can cause them to have disadvantage on their next attack against a creature that can see or hear you.

Predict Movement. You deduce where they are planning to move on their next turn. They can choose to change their plans, but if they move anywhere else, their movement speed is reduced by 10 feet.

Outwit Response. You can find their openings, negating their ability to use their reaction until the end of their next turn.

Expose Weakness. You can use Helpful Word to grant advantage against that target as part of the bonus action without expending a Leadership Die.

docs.title: Level 3 – Tactical Flexibility
docs.text: Additionally at 3rd level, you gain the ability to use Tactical Insight, Rallying Mark, Helpful Word, and Urgent Orders as an action or a bonus action on your turn.

docs.title: Level 7 – Inscrutable Mind
docs.text: Starting at 7th level, you gain proficiency in Intelligence Saving Throws. Additionally, as a reaction when being forced to make a Wisdom, Intelligence, or Charisma Saving Throw, you can expend one Leadership Die and add the die result to the saving throw.

docs.title: Level 7 – Control the Field
docs.text:
Starting at 7th level, when you use an ability that moves allied creatures (such as Urgent Orders or Shift the Field), it gains the following properties:

Deceptive Movement. You can attempt to move creatures that are not allies up to 5 feet (or half their movement speed, whichever is less). The creature must make an Intelligence Saving Throw with a DC of 8 + your Intelligence modifier + your proficiency bonus, or feel compelled to move immediately.

Flanking Maneuvers. If two allies you move are on opposite sides of a creature after the movement you grant, the first one to attack that enemy has advantage on their first attack if they attack before the creature moves.

Coordinated Transitions. Allies can move through each other's spaces during the movement you grant without it being difficult terrain.

docs.title: Level 11 – Tactical Strike
docs.text: Starting at 11th level, when you succeed on a Tactical Insight check against a creature, the next time you or a friendly creature deal damage against it before the start of your next turn it is increased by 2d6 damage.

docs.title: Level 15 – Advanced Orders
docs.text: Additionally at 15th level, when you expend Leadership Die on Urgent Orders, you can allow the creature to take one of the Use an Object, Search, Hide, or Dodge actions as their reaction instead of moving.

docs.title: Level 18 – Unstoppable Schemes
docs.text: Starting at 18th level, standing in your way becomes a pointless endeavor. When you move your allies with Urgent Orders or Shift the Field, they can move through spaces occupied by hostile creatures so long as they do not end their movement in an occupied space.

docs.title: Level 18 – Multilayered Tactics
docs.text: Additionally at 18th level, when you succeed on a Tactical Insight check against a creature, you can choose two of the listed effects.

docs.title: The Blood Hunter
docs.text:
Blood Hunters are warriors who have undergone a dark alchemical ritual known as the Hunter's Bane, suffusing their blood with sinister magic to combat the monsters that prey upon the innocent. They harness ancient Blood Rites, sacrifice their own vitality to fuel deadly effects, and join secretive Occult Orders that shape their methods of monster-slaying.

Progression TableCore Blood Hunter FeaturesBlood RitesBlood Hunter Orders

Choose a blood hunter order:

Order of Alchemists

Blood Hunters that join this Order make use of dark alchemy and transmutation magic to mutate their physical form. The sinister power in their blood triggers massive physiological changes thanks to experimental Mutagens. These mutants enhance their mortal form to meet monsters as their peer.
